title: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the …
body: US-001 AC3 ([oracle: file-assert git check-ignore -q on each path token of the edited bullet exits non-zero]) is structurally vacuous: line 901 contains zero path tokens, so the loop body never executes and the oracle passes with zero iterations. The intent (no gitignored path token in the bullet) is satisfied, but a zero-match sweep passing silently is the same self-nullifying shape the bullet at patterns.md:901 warns about. Consider asserting a non-zero token count before iterating.

title: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` …
body: Worth capturing as a bullet: the review/measurement shell is zsh, where `$c:t` and `$c:s` are path modifiers, so a loop written as `git show "$c:test/foo.ts"` silently expands to `<sha>est/foo.ts` and, with stderr redirected, yields an empty file and a bogus `grep -c` of 0 for every commit. This produced two wrong measurements during this review and is the unidentified cause of the 'for-loop pipeline gave inconsistent readings' note in the round-2 artifact. Per-commit sweeps should run under an explicit `bash -c`.

body: fixtureBody (247-248) and expectedBody (258-259) are byte-identical literals; a single shared const would remove the duplicate string while preserving the hand-pinned (non-regex-derived) guarantee. Cosmetic only, non-blocking.

title: The new test covers only the fence-breakout (bug) case. The happy-path default …
body: The new test covers only the fence-breakout (bug) case. The happy-path default (a diff with no backtick runs keeping the conventional 3-backtick fence) is exercised only indirectly by sibling tests; an explicit assertion that longestBacktickRun=0 yields a length-3 fence would lock the max(3, ...) floor directly.

title: promote does not dedup its input fingerprint list: `cam suggestions promote fp1…
body: promote does not dedup its input fingerprint list: `cam suggestions promote fp1 fp1` would emit two identical suggestion-fingerprint blocks in the composite issue while removeSuggestionLines drops the line once (second removal is a no-op). Not spec-required, but a Set over `fingerprints` before building entries would harden the edge case.

title: The composite-promote test promotes both pen entries, so it never exercises byt…
body: The composite-promote test promotes both pen entries, so it never exercises byte-preservation of a NON-promoted line during a variadic promote. removeSuggestionLines reuses the well-tested byte-preserving removeSuggestionLine, so coverage is indirect; a fixture with a third untouched entry would assert AC #2's byte-preservation clause directly for the composite path.

title: The stderr-capture assertions were moved inside the withFakeClock callback (Sit…
body: The stderr-capture assertions were moved inside the withFakeClock callback (Site A lines ~341-343, Site B AC4 ~line 745), so they execute while process.stderr.write is still patched. On assertion failure the framework's diff output routes into the captured chunks rather than the real terminal, which can obscure failure diagnostics. Consider exposing the captured chunks after the helper returns (or asserting outside the callback) so failures print normally. Non-blocking: restore is guaranteed by the finally, and all tests pass.

title: The self-pid write is placed before runContainerEnsureGuard's early-return, so …
body: The self-pid write is placed before runContainerEnsureGuard's early-return, so in container mode the host sidecar's pid is written to .claude even though the function returns early. This mirrors the existing writeSessionStartFn placement and matches the spec, so it is not a defect; a future note could clarify whether the container path wants its own liveness marker.

title: The pre-existing 'AC2: no historical data at all' test uses writePrd(cwd, 1), s…
body: The pre-existing 'AC2: no historical data at all' test uses writePrd(cwd, 1), so with the new storyCount <= 1 guard it now short-circuits at the guard before ever exercising the empty-history/aggregate branch it was written to cover. Bumping its prd to storyCount 2 would restore the branch it intends to verify. Non-blocking: the assertion (zero notify/events) still holds.
